steps.title: The last cookie
paragraphs: There was one cookie left on the plate. Ben grabbed it, stuffed it in his mouth and said, "What? I was hungry."
His little sister Ana looked at the empty plate. Then she broke her own cookie in half and gave a piece to the dog.
Nobody told you that Ben is selfish or that Ana is kind. But you know, don't you? Their actions told you.

cards.title: Traits
cards.body: A trait is part of a character's personality: brave, shy, stubborn, kind, curious. Telling names the trait. Showing lets the reader work it out from what the character does, says and chooses.

cards.title: Tell it or show it
cards.showing: When the dog growled at her little brother, Maya stepped in front of him and held out her hand, palm up.
cards.note: The second version never says "brave", but you saw it happen.

cards.title: Choices show the most
cards.body: The strongest way to show a trait is a choice, especially a hard one. Does your character share the last slice, or keep it? Tell the truth, or hide the broken vase? Readers learn who a character is from what they choose.

cards.title: Find the clues
cards.prompt: Tap the three action words that show Leo is curious.
cards.text: Leo peeked under the tarp, poked the strange box with a stick, and pressed his ear against the lid.

prompts: Copy the action you are proudest of. Which trait does it show?
Could Quill's reader tell the traits you picked? What would you change?
